title: Hospital Bills and Fee Benchmarks
summary: MOH fee benchmarks are reference ranges for routine and typical private-sector cases. Separate ranges may apply to hospital charges and doctors' professional fees, and the benchmarks do not apply to public hospitals.
guidance: Ask the doctor or hospital for the TOSP code or provisional diagnosis and an itemised fee breakdown.
A benchmark is not a quote; complexity and the actual care delivered can change the final bill.
Hospital fee benchmarks and professional fee benchmarks cover different bill components.

title: Getting medical help
summary: MOH advises using community care such as a GP or polyclinic for mild-to-moderate symptoms and going to an Emergency Department when there are signs of a medical emergency.
guidance: Emergency warning signs listed by MOH include sudden or severe pain, breathing difficulty, uncontrolled bleeding, sudden confusion, and sudden weakness or vision change.
A clinician should assess symptoms and decide whether tests, procedures, or referral are appropriate.

title: Conditions
summary: MOH's Conditions directory links to guidance for selected common health conditions, including abdominal pain or indigestion, cold and flu, diarrhoea and vomiting, fever, headaches, high blood pressure, hives, skin infections, and strains or sprains.
guidance: Use the condition-specific MOH page, where available, to understand common symptoms and when to seek medical care.
A directory listing is general information and does not establish a diagnosis or replace an individual clinical assessment.

title: Visiting a pharmacist
summary: MOH describes pharmacists as healthcare partners who can advise on medication use, side effects, storage, and possible food, medicine, supplement, or traditional-medicine interactions. Pharmacists can also advise on managing common health conditions.
guidance: Tell the pharmacist about allergies, other medical conditions, and medicines you are taking when seeking medication advice.
Ask a pharmacist about a medicine's purpose, how to take it, common side effects, storage, and relevant precautions.

title: Seeking a doctor
summary: MOH advises that GPs can treat many conditions and that people with mild-to-moderate health problems should consider seeing a GP first, allowing Emergency Departments to focus on more urgent cases. A GP can assess the problem and refer onward when appropriate.
guidance: A GP can assess symptoms, advise on next steps, and decide whether referral, tests, or more urgent care are appropriate.
Do not use this general GP-first guidance to delay emergency care when emergency warning signs are present.

title: When to visit the hospital for emergencies
summary: MOH describes a medical emergency as a sudden illness requiring immediate attention. Its warning signs include sudden or severe pain, breathing difficulty, uncontrolled bleeding, sudden confusion, sudden dizziness, numbness, weakness or vision change, coughing or vomiting blood, and continuous vomiting or diarrhoea.
guidance: Seek immediate medical attention for a possible medical emergency.
Keep identification, a current medicine list, and relevant contact details available when preparing for an emergency.

title: Find a Condition
summary: NUHS provides a searchable directory of diseases and conditions treated at its institutions. NUHS notes that the directory is a guide and not a complete list of conditions treated.
guidance: Use the directory to find relevant patient-education material or a treating institution, not to self-diagnose.
The directory does not establish that a person has a condition or that a particular treatment is appropriate.

title: Symptoms & Medical Conditions
summary: SingHealth provides an A-Z and body-region directory of patient information on symptoms and medical conditions, including information categories such as symptoms, causes, diagnosis, and treatments.
guidance: Use condition pages as general patient education and discuss symptoms, tests, and treatment choices with a qualified clinician.
A condition directory cannot diagnose an individual or replace professional medical advice.

title: Conditions & Diseases
summary: Mount Elizabeth Hospitals provides a Conditions & Diseases directory as supplementary patient education.
guidance: Use this directory to locate general educational material, not as a diagnosis or individual treatment recommendation.

title: Conditions & Diseases
summary: Gleneagles Hospital Singapore provides a Conditions & Diseases directory as supplementary patient education.
guidance: Use this directory to locate general educational material, not as a diagnosis or individual treatment recommendation.

title: Emergency Medical Services
summary: SCDF operates Singapore's 24-hour Emergency Medical Services. Call 995 for life-threatening emergencies such as cardiac arrest, seizures, breathlessness, loss of consciousness, excessive bleeding, major trauma, or stroke.
guidance: Call 995 for a life-threatening emergency and follow the call-taker's instructions.
Describe the person's signs and symptoms briefly and provide the exact location.
